10.1016_j.jnucmat.2026.156651: Copper has been selected to provide corrosion resistance for containers that will house spent nuclear fuel in deep geological repositories in Canada and elsewhere. Corrosion estimates generally assume that the pre-emplacement period, and those time periods immediately following emplacement, will result in very minimal corrosion of the copper layer, allowing these periods to be ignored in lifetime total corrosion damage calculations. However, when metallic containers are exposed to moist bentonite buffer components, it is possible that conditions could be favourable for some corrosion to occur, leading to the formation of corrosion damage and oxide coatings that could alter corrosion behaviour later in the repository lifecycle. Here, experiments conducted in high humidity atmospheres (98% relative humidity) with moist (20% gravimetric moisture content), compacted bentonite showed that copper corrosion can be enhanced by bentonite contact. The corrosion rate was found to decrease over time, but the rate was consistently higher in the bentonite exposure conditions. Greater penetration depths were also found in bentonite exposed samples. A high degree of heterogeneity was observed on the samples throughout the exposure, with some areas being nearly completely uncorroded and others having hundreds of nanometers of penetration. This indicates that the pre- and early-emplacement periods may need to be included when considering the total damage of the copper container.
10.1021_acsnano.6c17118: We demonstrate a flexible nanofibrous membrane featuring a valley-cell array (NMVA). Inspired by honeycombs and spider silk, the NMVA is rationally designed using poly(vinyl alcohol), carbon black, and MOF-303 as its main components. The synergistic effect of the flexible honeycomb network, abundant hydrophilic sites of MOF-decorated nanofibers, rapid photothermal response, and multidimensional structural stability favors highly efficient adsorption and desorption dynamics during water harvesting. The valleys of the honeycomb cell arrays enhance light capture for photothermal conversion and water release, while the abundant hydrophilic sites facilitate water molecule capture and uptake. As a result, NMVA achieves a high water uptake capacity of ∼0.41 g g-1 at 25 °C and 30% RH, and can release 92% of the absorbed water within 30 min under 1 sun irradiation. For an integrated NMVA in outdoor conditions under sunlight of ∼0.76 kW m-2 on average, water harvesting capacities reach 3.85-5.0 L kg-1 day-1 at 42-68% RH through continuous all-day water uptake-release over seven cycles. This study provides insights into the design of novel materials that can be extended into the realms of water engineering for energy systems and portable devices.
10.1109_led.2026.3748589: Physical reservoir computing (RC) leveraging emerging synaptic devices with inherent nonlinearity and short-term plasticity enables efficient temporal information processing with low training cost. However, most reported devices are resistive, and their reservoir states are read out via current fluxes, which inevitably incurs substantial power consumption and hardware overhead. In this letter, we propose a capacitive synaptic device based on a Ti/LiPON/Ti supercapacitor. Driven by the coupled dynamics of Li+migration and spontaneous back-diffusion, the device exhibits nonlinear and short-term synaptic behaviors, including excitatory post-synaptic potential and paired-pulse facilitation, with excellent cycling stability (variation as low as 0.24%), making it suitable for RC. Unlike resistive counterparts, the capacitive synapse allows reservoir states to be read out via its open-circuit voltage, achieving near-zero device-end readout power and eliminating current-to-voltage converters, thereby significantly reducing power consumption and hardware overhead. Notably, the symmetric architecture offers bidirectional ion dynamics, enabling native processing of bipolar signals. As a proof of concept, the device serves as physical reservoir nodes for the electrocardiogram recognition task, achieving 95.19% accuracy with device variability and readout noise included. This work provides a promising pathway toward compact, low-power RC hardware for encoding naturally bipolar temporal signals.
